level1.text: The thickness of a human hair is $82\,\mu\text{m}$. Give the thickness in millimetres.
The distance of the Moon from the Earth is on average $384\,400\,\text{km}$. Give the distance in megametres, when $1\,\text{Mm} = 10^{6}\,\text{m}$.
The length of a table is $1.85\,\text{m}$ and its width $0.92\,\text{m}$. Calculate the area of the table to as many significant figures as the measurement results justify.
In the picture an aluminium rod is next to a ruler. How long is the rod? Give the length in millimetres.

The diameter of the Moon is $3474\,\text{km}$, and it is drawn in a picture as one pixel wide. A circle corresponding to the Sun is drawn to the same scale. The diameter of the Sun is $1.392\cdot10^{6}\,\text{km}$. How many pixels wide is the Sun?
Which of the following units is a base unit of the SI system?

choices.feedback: The newton is a derived unit: it is obtained from base units as a product and a quotient, $1\,\text{N} = 1\,\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}^2$. There are only seven base units, and the unit of force is not one of them.
Correct: the SI base unit of mass is the kilogram. Of the base units it is the only one whose name already contains a prefix, kilo.
The gram is not a base unit of its own but a part of the kilogram formed with a prefix, $1\,\text{g} = 10^{-3}\,\text{kg}$. The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram.

Volume is a derived quantity, because it is obtained as a product of lengths, and its SI unit is $\text{m}^3$. The litre is not an SI unit but a unit used alongside it, $1\,\textsf{l} = 10^{-3}\,\text{m}^3$.

level1.text: A cyclist's speed is $18\,\text{km/h}$. Give the speed in the unit $\text{m/s}$.
Density is calculated with the formula $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$, where $m$ is the mass and $V$ the volume. What is the unit of density when the mass is in kilograms and the volume in cubic metres?
level1.answer: $\text{kg/m}^3$, because mass is divided by volume

choices.text: $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^3$, because mass and volume are multiplied
choices.feedback: In the formula the mass is divided by the volume, so the units are divided too: the kilogram goes in the numerator and the cubic metre in the denominator. The unit of a product would describe a completely different quantity.

choices.text: $\text{m}^3/\text{kg}$, because the volume is written first
choices.feedback: Units follow the order of the formula: $m$ is in the numerator, so its unit is in the numerator. The inverse unit $\text{m}^3/\text{kg}$ would tell how large a volume there is per kilogram.

choices.text: $\text{kg/m}^2$, because volume is measured in square metres
choices.feedback: The square metre is a unit of area. Volume is a product of three lengths, so its unit is $\text{m}\cdot\text{m}\cdot\text{m} = \text{m}^3$.

choices.text: $\text{kg/m}^3$, because mass is divided by volume
choices.feedback: Correct: the unit is obtained by substituting the units of the quantities into the formula. The unit of mass, $\text{kg}$, is divided by the unit of volume, $\text{m}^3$, so the unit of density is $\text{kg/m}^3$.

level2.text: The clock frequency of a computer processor is $3.2\,\text{GHz}$, that is 3.2 billion cycles per second. Use the values $1\,\text{GHz} = 10^{9}\,\text{Hz}$ and $1\,\text{Hz} = 1/\text{s}$. How many clock cycles can the processor perform in $5.0\,\text{ms}$?
The length of a bacterium is $2.0\,\mu\text{m}$. How many such bacteria fit one after another along a distance of $1.0\,\text{mm}$?
The area of a field is $2.4\,\text{km}^2$. Give the area in hectares, when $1\,\text{ha} = 10\,000\,\text{m}^2$.
The speed of Voyager 2 is $15.341\,\text{km/s}$. Assume the speed is constant. How many million kilometres does the probe travel in a day?
The table shows the speeds of four vehicles in different units. Use the value $1\,\text{knot} = 1.852\,\text{km/h}$. Which vehicle is the fastest? Give its speed in the unit $\text{m/s}$.
A student weighed five apples of the same variety and recorded the results in a table. Find the error in the table and correct it. Then calculate the mean mass of an apple in kilograms.

A tap fills a bucket at a steady flow rate $q = 0.20\,\textsf{l}/\text{s}$. A student calculates how long it takes to fill a $12\,\textsf{l}$ bucket.

The student's solution is: “The time is the product of the flow rate and the volume, $t = qV = 0.20\,\textsf{l}/\text{s}\cdot12\,\textsf{l} = 2.4$.” The student concludes that the bucket fills in $2.4$ seconds.

Check the units of the student's calculation and explain what a unit check reveals about the error. Then calculate the correct time in minutes.

level3.text: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year. Use the values $c = 2.998\cdot10^{5}\,\text{km/s}$, $1\,\text{a} = 3.156\cdot10^{7}\,\text{s}$ and $1\,\text{AU} = 1.496\cdot10^{8}\,\text{km}$. How many astronomical units is one light-year?

The width of a screen is exactly $1920\,\text{px}$. In a picture the diameter of the Moon, $3474\,\text{km}$, is one pixel. From the Sun to Neptune is $30.07\,\text{AU}$ and $1\,\text{AU} = 1.496\cdot10^{8}\,\text{km}$. How many screen widths side by side are needed for the distance from the Sun to Neptune to fit in the picture?

A control centre sends a command to Voyager 2 when the probe is $145\,\text{AU}$ away. The command travels at the speed of light, and the probe sends a confirmation straight back. Use the values $1\,\text{AU} = 1.496\cdot10^{8}\,\text{km}$ and $c = 2.998\cdot10^{5}\,\text{km/s}$. How many hours pass from sending the command to the arrival of the confirmation?

The period $T$ of a pendulum, that is the time of one full swing, can depend only on the length $L$ of the pendulum, the acceleration of free fall $g$ and the mass $m$ of the pendulum.

Assume that $T = k\,L^{a}g^{b}m^{c}$, where $k$ is a number without a unit. Use the units to deduce the exponents $a$, $b$ and $c$.

With a length of $0.250\,\text{m}$ the period was measured to be $1.00\,\text{s}$. How long is the period in the same place when the length is $1.00\,\text{m}$?

A manufacturer gives the specifications of two portable power banks in different units. Both are fully charged, and each powers a device whose power is the operating power in the table.

The operating time is $t = \dfrac{E}{P}$, and for power $1\,\text{W} = 1\,\text{J/s}$. For units of energy $1\,\text{kWh} = 3.6\,\text{MJ}$.

Your friend claims that device B lasts longer because the numerical value of its energy, $2.20$, is larger than the value $0.65$ of device A.

How many hours longer does the longer-lasting device run? Justify. Is the claim correct?
